title: basic-auth LogMetric/LogBatch metric routing: a per-metric model_id needs UPDATE on that logged model, not just on the run
answers: Why does log-metric or log-batch return 403 for a user who can update the run when a metric has a model_id?
A user with UPDATE on their run could write metrics onto another user's LoggedModel; where is that blocked?
Where is the permission check for the model_id field and its modelId alias on metric logging?
Batch logging with several metrics targeting different logged models is denied when one model is not writable; why?
body:
Path: Metric logging in the basic-auth app, `POST /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-metric` (LogMetric) and `POST /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-batch` (LogBatch), where an optional `model_id` on a metric routes the value onto a LoggedModel. The chokepoints are `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_log_metric` and `validate_can_log_batch`, both feeding `_validate_can_update_run_and_models`.
Rule: The check requires UPDATE on the run (`_get_permission_from_run_id`) and UPDATE on every distinct non-empty `model_id` the request references. Model IDs are read from the proto parse, so the camelCase `modelId` alias is covered. Each id is checked through `_get_model_permission(model_id)`, which `_get_permission_from_model_id` now delegates to. Any single unwritable model denies the whole request.
Symptom: A user with UPDATE on their own run could attach metric records to any LoggedModel in the instance by passing its id as `model_id` (GHSA-j6gw-m35q-8j63); the endpoints checked only the run.
Constraints: Only LogMetric and LogBatch are covered; other run-scoped writes that accept a model id still use `validate_can_update_run`. A nonexistent model_id (RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST) returns the same 403 as a denied one, to avoid an existence oracle; other MlflowExceptions propagate. Requests with no model_id need only run UPDATE. Each distinct model costs a serial model lookup plus permission resolution, and a bulk lookup was deferred as a follow-up.
Applies: Authorization for log-metric and log-batch in the basic-auth app whenever metrics carry a model_id, including the modelId alias.
applies: Basic-auth app metric logging (LogMetric/LogBatch) with a model_id on any metric; not for run-only metric writes.
says: Logging metrics against a run fails with access denied when referencing a model.
Prevent users from attaching experiment metrics to logged models they do not own.
Batch metric logging fails completely if even one targeted model cannot be edited.
Users should not be allowed to record evaluation metrics onto another member's model.
search: In the basic-auth app, POST /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-metric (LogMetric) and POST /api/2.0/mlflow/runs/log-batch (LogBatch) route through validate_can_log_metric and validate_can_log_batch into _validate_can_update_run_and_models, requiring UPDATE on the run and UPDATE on each distinct model_id. Model IDs are parsed from protobuf (including the camelCase modelId alias) and checked via _get_model_permission(model_id), where any unwritable or missing (RESOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST) model denies the request with a 403 status. Requests without a model_id require only run UPDATE, and other run-scoped write endpoints continue using validate_can_update_run. Covers LogMetric and LogBatch under basic-auth, deferring bulk model lookup as noted in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py:test_log_batch_model_id_requires_update.
